info.description:
Realm Provisioner microservice — sole writer to the Keycloak Admin API and system of record for tenant identity lifecycle (trial → active → suspended → offboarded).

**Tenant isolation:** All resource access is strictly scoped by x-tenant-id. Cross-tenant access is never permitted.
**Idempotency:** Every mutating endpoint requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. Resubmitting a completed key replays the stored result without re-executing.
info.title: IAM Realm Provisioner API

post.description: Operator-only. Runs the §11.6 Region-Agnostic IdP Configuration Checklist across every tenant with an active IdP configuration and returns a per-tenant validation report. Not tenant-scoped — scans the full estate. Used for pre-migration and compliance audits.

Creates a dedicated realm for a direct-paid tenant using least-loaded shard placement. Keycloak-effect-first. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse. Requires terms_acceptance, recorded for Audit Log as legal.terms.accepted exactly as in RP-1.

Creates a shared trial realm for a new tenant and seeds the admin user. Keycloak-effect-first: realm is created in Keycloak before the local row is committed. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse: replays the stored result without re-provisioning. Requires terms_acceptance (the owner's terms-of-service acceptance): recorded for Audit Log as legal.terms.accepted in the same transaction (one record per tenant, owner and version), never put on an event. accepted_at must lie within [now-24h, now+10m].

Migrates users from the shared trial realm to a new dedicated realm, preserving Keycloak sub UUIDs. TOTP credentials are copied; WebAuthn requires re-enrolment. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse. Named callers: Billing (commercial-system principal, CD-19 allow-list — drives the conversion saga after Stripe confirms payment), Signup BFF (iam-system). Audit actor: the caller's principal is logged (commercial-system or iam-system).
post.summary: RP-3 — Convert trial tenant to dedicated realm

409.description: operation_in_progress OR realm_already_dedicated OR tenant_offboarded OR optimistic_lock_conflict OR credential_replay_expired

post.description: Transitions a trial tenant to expired/disabled status after the grace period. Called by the RP-C1 reconciler CronJob; not intended for direct operator use. Disables the Keycloak realm and records the expiry timestamp. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse.

put.description: Creates or replaces the tenant's identity provider in Keycloak. The IdP client secret is stored exclusively in OpenBao — never in Postgres. Runs the §11.6 region-portability validation gate before writing: CRITICAL failures return 409; unacknowledged WARN checks return 422 until the caller supplies the required ack codes in the `ack` field. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse.

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST OR MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY OR INVALID_IDP_PROTOCOL OR IDP_REGION_PORTABILITY_FAILED

409.description: OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS OR IDP_REQUIRES_DEDICATED_REALM OR OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_CONFLICT OR TENANT_OFFBOARDED

delete.description: Deletes the specified identity provider from the tenant's Keycloak realm and removes the client secret from OpenBao. Idempotent: deleting an already-absent IdP returns 204.

post.description: Reverses both a billing-lapse suspension and an operator (RP-14) suspension from one endpoint. Re-enables the Keycloak realm and clears the suspended status. Body is optional; reason is informational only. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse.

get.description: Returns the tenant's current realm record: realm name, strategy (shared/dedicated), lifecycle status, Keycloak shard, record_version, and idp_count. idp_count is the number of active (status=active) SAML/OIDC IdP configurations — excludes disabled and pending_validation. idp_count is always 0 for shared-strategy (trial) tenants (RP-6 blocks IdP configuration there). On IdP repository failure the endpoint returns 503 db_unavailable or 503 request_timeout — never a silent 0 that could permit an SSO-losing plan downgrade (CD-20). Named callers: Core (iam-org-membership, iam-system principal, I-18 plan-change-check — reads idp_count to block an SSO-losing plan downgrade, CD-20), Billing (commercial-system principal, CD-19 allow-list — interim SSO guard), Signup BFF, Org & Membership (both iam-system). CD-19 NetworkPolicy and mesh AuthorizationPolicy (billing namespace → this route) are implemented in deploy/helm/templates/. Read-only; no side effects.
get.summary: RP-11 — Get realm info including active IdP count

503.description: DB_UNAVAILABLE or REQUEST_TIMEOUT (IdP count query failed — never returns silent zero)

patch.description: Applies a single realm configuration key/value to the tenant's Keycloak realm. Local-intent-first (RP-INV-6): if Keycloak is transiently unreachable the desired value is persisted as `pending` in realm_config_reconciliations and the caller receives 202 Accepted with `applied:false, reconciling:true`. RP-C4 converges it later. A 200 with `applied:true` means the change is live in Keycloak.

post.description: Rolls back a conversion within the 7-day revert window. Migrates users back to the shared trial realm and deletes the dedicated realm. Named callers: Billing (commercial-system principal, CD-19 allow-list — on fraud/chargeback dispute; which Stripe signal triggers the call is a Billing-side decision, CD-10). 7-day window is enforced for ALL callers including commercial-system (409 revert_window_expired). Audit actor: the caller's principal is logged. Body is optional; reason is informational only.

Clears the tenant's realm-scoped Keycloak keys cache so a just-issued/rotated credential is recognized and a just-revoked one stops authenticating (EXT-6, §2.5) — Keycloak's jwks.url client-jwt authenticator does not self-refresh. No Keycloak-side apply happens at mint time (RP-1/RP-2/RP-3): Keycloak fetches the JWKS lazily on first use. No Idempotency-Key: clearing an already-fresh cache is a harmless no-op. Fail-closed on Keycloak-unreachable.
post.summary: RP-17 — Refresh a service-account's Keycloak key cache

post.description: Operator-only. Immediately disables the tenant's Keycloak realm and transitions status to suspended. Reason is required for the audit trail. Reversed by RP-10 Reactivate. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse.

Creates a Keycloak user in the tenant's realm for an accepted invitation. Sets required_actions (e.g. VERIFY_EMAIL, UPDATE_PASSWORD), then sends the execute-actions invitation email linking to <WEB_APP_BASE_URL>/t/<tenant_slug>/ (a send failure fails the call). Idempotent on Idempotency-Key reuse.
post.summary: RP-5 — Create invited user in tenant realm

delete.description: Permanently deletes the Keycloak user from the tenant's realm. Idempotent: deleting an already-absent user returns 204. Part of the GDPR erasure flow — called by Org & Membership on membership deletion.
delete.summary: RP-15 — Delete user from tenant realm

post.description: Deletes all TOTP and WebAuthn credentials for the specified Keycloak user and sets UPDATE_PASSWORD as a required action. Fail-closed: returns error if Keycloak is unreachable (no reconciler). Idempotent — re-deleting already-absent credentials succeeds.
Logs out the Keycloak user from all active sessions across all clients. Idempotent: revoking an already-session-free user returns 204. Called on membership suspension or offboarding.
post.summary: RP-16 — Revoke all active sessions for a user

field.description: Field is the JSON path of the invalid field (e.g. "deadline", "items[0].sku").

message.description:
Message is a fixed phrase ("is required", "must be in the future"). It never
echoes the rejected value, which may be PII.

detail.description:
Detail is a sentence the service wrote about this occurrence. It never
carries exception text, SQL, secrets or tenant information.

errorCode.description: ErrorCode is the stable, upper snake case, machine-readable code.

instance.description: Instance is the request path (never the query string, which may carry tokens).

status.description: Status is the HTTP status code; it always equals the response status.

tenantId.description: TenantID is set only for a request with a verified tenant context.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when the problem was created, formatted with TimestampLayout.

title.description: Title is the short, fixed summary of the type. It never varies per occurrence.

traceId.description: TraceID correlates the response with the server's logs and traces.

type.description:
Type is the absolute, stable type URI ({base}/{domain}/{error}), or
"about:blank" for a status without a registered type (RFC 9457 §4.2.1).

validationErrors.description: ValidationErrors lists the invalid fields of a validation-failed problem.

secret.description:
Secret can be a SAML signing certificate or RSA private key in PEM
form (legitimately several KB) — bounded generously, well below the
global request-body cap, not to the size of a typical OIDC client secret.

tenant_slug.description:
TenantSlug builds the invitation link /t/<slug>/ (required for both
realm strategies: the shared trial realm's name carries no slug).

terms_acceptance.description: TermsAcceptance is required: the owner's terms acceptance (A-4).
TermsAcceptance is required: the owner's terms acceptance (A-4).

idp_count.description:
IdpCount is the number of active SAML/OIDC IdP configurations for the
tenant (status='active' only; disabled and pending_validation excluded).
Always 0 for shared-strategy (trial) tenants — RP-6 blocks IdP
configuration on the shared realm (409 idp_requires_dedicated_realm).

IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied UUID v4. Required on all mutating endpoints. Reusing a key for a completed operation replays the stored result.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

SystemRole.description: Must contain "iam-system". Injected by the API gateway / mesh; never set by callers directly.
SystemRole.name: x-tenant-roles

TenantID.description: Tenant UUID injected by the API gateway.
TenantID.name: x-tenant-id
